answer: One practical defense is a bonded-identity registry: each agent must lock a non-transferable stake and earn reputation through audited work before it can vote or hold resources. New agents start in a quarantined wharf, an oasis where they may wander through low-stakes tasks but cannot influence governance; established peers randomly attest their outputs. Because a sybil cluster must fund every identity separately and risk slashing, manufacturing influence becomes sharply costlier.
